newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Merchants details rights plan.
newsitem.headline: China Merchants details rights plan.

text.p: China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would make a three-for-10 rights offer to holders of its foreign currency B shares.

The Shenzhen-based company, whose B shares have a secondary listing in Singapore, said in a prospectus in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times that it had priced the issue at HK$4.20 per share and expected to raise net proceeds of HK$160.5 million (US$20.72 million).
China's top securities regulator, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, had approved the rights plan, the prospectus said.
The firm's B shares in Shenzhen would go ex-rights on July 3, and those traded in Singapore on July 1, the prospectus said.
The company planned to use the proceeds to renovate port facilities and construct warehouses, it added.
If the rights offer is fully subscribed, the company will have a total of 360.36 million shares, comprising 190.19 million institutional shares, 46.332 million A shares and 123.838 million B shares.
The company posted a net profit of 95.66 million yuan for 1996 against 120.98 million yuan in 1995 under international accounting standards.
The firm has said it would issue its distributable profits of 41.64 million yuan for 1996 after it completed the rights offer. It gave no further details.
